_about: Exact redirect changes required at the Cloudflare edge to give each money-market
head intent a single primary URL with no 301 -> rel=canonical two-hop.
NOTHING IN THIS FILE IS DEPLOYED. It is a deployment request, reviewed in git and
applied by hand in the Cloudflare dashboard per RUNBOOK.md. This repository has no
mechanism that can change edge routing: GitHub Pages serves the tree and does not
read vercel.json, and .github/ is not served at all.
Set activated to true only after RUNBOOK.md step 7 confirms the edge matches. The
canonical-verify gate FAILS if activated is true, on purpose: flipping it is a
deliberate, reviewable act that must accompany the runbook's verification output.

target.mechanism: Bulk Redirects (Rules > Redirect Rules > Bulk Redirects)

mirror.method: HEAD probe of 612 URLs with redirects disabled
mirror.result: 69/69 rules matched the edge exactly; 0 live 301s absent from the file; server=cloudflare on every response
mirror.note: vercel.json is an observed mirror only. After applying these rules, update vercel.json in a follow-up commit so the mirror stays accurate. Updating it is bookkeeping, not deployment.

rules.defect: Broad commercial-glazing slug resolves to a storefront primary in two hops: 301 to /miami/ (title 'Storefront Glazier in Miami, FL - Service Area'), which rel=canonicals to /storefront-glazier-miami-florida/.
rules.after: One hop, landing on the ratified commercial-glazing primary, which is self-canonical.

rules.defect: Same two-hop as Miami: 301 to /tampa/ (storefront copy), which rel=canonicals to /storefront-glazier-tampa-florida/.
rules.after: One hop, landing on the ratified commercial-glazing primary, which is self-canonical.

deliberately_not_requested.detail: West Palm Beach holds #1 organic and #1 map. Which of the four WPB URLs holds the organic #1 is not measurable from this workspace, and the two research documents disagree on which should be primary. No WPB routing change is requested.

No /orlando-commercial-glazing.html exists. Flattening this onto /storefront-glazier-orlando-florida/ would be exactly the storefront-as-broad-primary error this workstream is reversing. Unblocked by creating the Orlando commercial-glazing hub, not by a redirect.

Consolidated in-repo by rel=canonical to /commercial-glazing-nashville-tn.html plus sitemap removal. A 301 would also work but is strictly worse here: acg_local_seo_maps_strategy_research_20260728.md Gate 5 wants /nashville/ available as a Google Business Profile landing page once the Q3 2026 office is real. A canonical keeps that option; a 301 destroys it.
Consolidated in-repo by rel=canonical to /tennessee-commercial-glazing/ plus sitemap removal.

Recorded as its own near-me intent. Folding it into /glazing-contractor-florida.html is a primary decision that needs a GSC baseline first. The superseded plan promoted it to statewide primary; that is reversed.
seo-targets.json labels this a second statewide-hub alongside /glazing-contractor-florida.html. Genuinely duplicative, but collapsing it flips a primary. Needs GSC.

Roughly 27 non-money-market cities carry the identical two-hop (Aventura, Boynton Beach, Coral Gables, Delray Beach, Fort Myers, Sarasota, St Petersburg, Stuart, Jupiter and others). The same objection applies: their /{city}/ pages are all storefront copy and no commercial-glazing hub exists for any of them. Out of scope for the 11 money markets; the fix is the same and should follow the same rule.

gate.static: Asserts this file exists, is not activated, covers exactly the registry's required redirects, and that current_destination still matches the vercel.json mirror.
gate.live: canonical-verify.py --live HEAD-probes all 69 mirror rules and fails on any divergence between the edge and vercel.json. Run this before and after applying the rules below.
